extracted.intended_audience: researchers, clinicians and policy-makers interested in the evidence for peer support interventions for people with severe mental illness; systematic reviewers and trialists in mental health
extracted.subtask_description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials of community-based peer support interventions for adults with severe mental illness, categorising interventions into mutual support, peer-support services, and peer-delivered services, and assessing outcomes and quality using Cochrane Risk of Bias and GRADE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of trials eligible
rubrics_metrics.description: Randomised controlled trials (RCTs) including cluster RCTs and factorial RCTs were included. Published and unpublished trials were eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclude non-randomised studies when the review aims to evaluate efficacy; include cluster and factorial designs; search without restriction by publication status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of participants (eligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies were included if participants were adults with severe mental illness (schizophrenia spectrum or bipolar disorder, or mixed populations of people using secondary mental health services). Studies including only unipolar depression or personality disorders were excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peers (providers) should be using or have used secondary mental health services. Report participant diagnoses, employment, comorbidity, age and sex; exclude studies that do not match the target clinical population.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of interventions (inclusion/exclusion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Included interventions were community-based peer support designed to facilitate recovery from severe mental illness. Excluded: residential and inpatient peer-run programmes; programmes focusing exclusively on other areas (employment, physical health, drug and alcohol use); interventions led by mental health professionals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include studies of peer support in addition to other interventions only if the effect of peer support can be isolated. When interventions mix peer and clinical components so that peer effect cannot be isolated, exclude from main analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervention typology / categorisation
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer support interventions were pre-defined and categorised as: (i) Mutual support groups (reciprocal relationships); (ii) Peer-support services (primarily uni-directional peer supporters offering support in addition to standard care); (iii) Peer mental health service providers (service users employed to provide part or all of standard care, where the difference from usual care is the provider).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these theoretically distinct subgroups to avoid inappropriate combination in meta-analysis; distinguish interventions where the provider vs the role differs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combining multiple interventions and comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: When studies included more than one eligible intervention, they were combined for analysis. When studies included multiple comparison groups, include all comparisons that allowed isolation of peer-provided effects (e.g., peer+TAU vs TAU; peer-led vs professionally-led services).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not analyse other groups that do not isolate the peer effect; be explicit about which arms are combined and why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcomes to evaluate
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary and secondary outcomes included objective outcomes (hospitalisation, employment) and self-reported outcomes (overall psychiatric symptoms, symptoms of psychosis, depression and anxiety, quality of life, recovery (self-rated), hope, empowerment, and satisfaction with services).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-specify main outcomes a priori but note that additional outcomes commonly reported (e.g., hope, empowerment) can be added post-hoc with transparency. Report outcomes at all time points where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search strategy standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Comprehensive searches of CENTRAL, CINAHL, Embase, Medline, preMedline, and PsycINFO from inception to date, combining synonyms for severe mental illness, peer support, and randomised controlled trial using AND; update searches; search reference lists; contact study authors and experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not restrict by publication status; document search strategies (appendices) and dates; update searches as part of broader reviews when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Screening process
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstracts were screened independently by two authors and differences were resolved with a third author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use independent dual screening to reduce selection bias and document procedures for resolving disagreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data extraction standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Data were extracted independently by two reviewers. Extract outcomes at all time points, study characteristics (setting, number randomised, duration), inclusion criteria and participant demographics, and characteristics of the interventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact authors for missing data and unpublished studies; record which outcomes/time points are available and which are not; extract intervention training/supervision details and delivery mode (face-to-face, internet).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of bias (risk of bias tool and domains)
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies were assessed using the Cochrane Collaboration Risk of Bias Tool. Two authors rated each study for risk of bias due to: sequence generation; allocation concealment; blinding of participants, assessors and providers; selective outcome reporting; and incomplete data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rate each domain as high (seriously weakens confidence), low (unlikely to seriously alter results) or unclear. Resolve discrepancies through discussion. Use bias assessments to inform GRADE downgrading and sensitivity analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of missing data
rubrics_metrics.description: Missing data were noted for each outcome. When dropout was not reported, authors were contacted. When analyses controlled for dropout (e.g., imputed using regression methods), these were used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer analyses that control for dropout (imputation) over completer analyses; transparently report missing outcome data and attrition bias judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical analysis methods
rubrics_metrics.description: For continuous outcomes calculate standardized mean difference (Hedges' g) and weight studies using the inverse of variance. For dichotomous outcomes calculate risk ratios and combine using the Mantel-Haenszel method. Use random-effects models and report 95% confidence intervals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convert reported metrics to common effect sizes where necessary; state methods for handling multiple arms and cluster designs; use appropriate weighting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment and thresholds for heterogeneity
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistical heterogeneity assessed by visual inspection of forest plots, Chi2 test (p value) and I2 statistic. Heterogeneity considered substantial if p < 0.10 and I2 > 50%. Differences between subgroups tested using Chi2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report I2 and Chi2 p-values for each pooled analysis; consider heterogeneity in GRADE downgrading and interpret pooled effect cautiously when heterogeneity high.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-analysis software and evidence grading
rubrics_metrics.description: Meta-analysis conducted using RevMan and a summary of results prepared using the GRADE system, which assesses confidence in the evidence attending to threats to internal validity, inconsistency, indirectness, imprecision, and reporting bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rate confidence in the evidence as high, moderate, low or very low. Explicitly state reasons for downgrading (e.g., 1Risk of bias, 2Inconsistency, 3Indirectness, 4Imprecision, 5Publication/Reporting Bias). Downgrade results with I2 > 50% for study quality when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling cluster randomised trials
rubrics_metrics.description: For cluster-randomised trials ensure whether standard deviations were adjusted for clustering; if not adjusted, the precision of effects and their weight in analysis may be overestimated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust analyses for clustering where possible; if unclear, interpret estimates cautiously and consider sensitivity analyses excluding such trials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitivity analyses for methodological concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct sensitivity analyses excluding trials with specific methodological concerns (e.g., cluster trial with low uptake of the intervention) to assess whether results materially change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sensitivity analyses to test robustness of pooled estimates to inclusion/exclusion of trials with high risk or atypical implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synthesis and reporting of pooled effects
rubrics_metrics.description: For each outcome report number of trials and participants, effect size with 95% CI, heterogeneity metrics (I2, Chi2 p), follow-up time points, and GRADE confidence rating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide tables summarizing pooled effects at post-treatment and follow-up; transparently note outcomes with insufficient or non-convertible data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation caution: equivalence vs no-significant-difference
rubrics_metrics.description: Lack of significant differences between active interventions in superiority-designed trials should not be assumed to demonstrate equivalence. Non-inferiority requires trials designed and powered to demonstrate non-inferiority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid concluding equivalence when trials are underpowered for non-inferiority; explicitly state design limitations when interpreting null findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial reporting standards and pre-registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Trials should adhere to CONSORT guidelines for reporting. Future trials should be registered in advance, publish their protocols, clearly state all outcomes and time points, describe the interventions provided, and report outcomes in full.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improve reporting quality (methods, outcomes, implementation details) to reduce selective reporting and enable inclusion in meta-analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for process evaluation and clear intervention models
rubrics_metrics.description: Trials of complex interventions should include a process evaluation to understand whether the programme was implemented as intended and the mechanisms by which effects are achieved. Develop and describe clear theory-based intervention models and fidelity criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe intervention content, training and supervision of peer providers, delivery mode (face-to-face vs internet), and degree of integration with services to facilitate interpretation and replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programme content and reporting (training/supervision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report organisation and content of programmes, manualisation vs less structured support, online vs face-to-face delivery, and arrangements for training and supervision of peer providers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between manualised self-management programmes and less structured befriending/advocacy; report any clinician involvement; provide sufficient detail to allow typology assignment and fidelity assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of non-randomised studies for efficacy
rubrics_metrics.description: In line with best practice guidelines for systematic reviews of efficacy, do not supplement randomised trial evidence with non-randomised trials because including other designs could lead to misleading results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge that exclusion limits the number of studies and generalizability but preserves internal validity; consider separate reviews for implementation/hypothesis-generating evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active procedures to detect reporting bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Check for selective outcome reporting by contacting trial authors and checking review protocols. Confirm which studies were free of selective outcome reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Downgrade confidence where selective reporting is suspected; search for unpublished trials and outcomes, and explicitly state suspected reporting bias in GRADE justifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome selection and post-hoc additions
rubrics_metrics.description: Main outcomes should be identified a priori, but additional outcomes that are commonly reported and considered important by triallists and service users (e.g., hope and empowerment) can be added post-hoc with transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report which outcomes were pre-specified and which added later; be cautious interpreting post-hoc outcomes due to multiplicity and selective reporting risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy/practice implication criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Current evidence must be sufficient and of adequate quality to support recommendations or mandatory requirements from policy makers for mental health services to provide peer support programmes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If evidence is insufficient or low quality, do not recommend mandatory implementation; where programmes are implemented, embed rigorous evaluations and research designs to determine effects.
